summary:
Plan of w237 (supervision r214-r216) in plan.md.
All three scenarios are red only on missing steps: one Given and four Thens, to go in tests/scenarios/supervision_faults_steps.py. Faults.checkout_changes already leaves out other initiatives' parts (d8f57cc8).
The file set is the coordinator's: that step module and scripts/supervise_faults.py. The second changes only under reading B below.
No existing test breaks (verified by search, notes part 3).
One question is left by conflicting requirements. i2's own rounds (gate, apply, formulate) run in the same `work run`. One that ends after i1's researcher writes .shop/work/i2/initiative.md has its own checkout check put the change back and fault it (r218). r215 and r216 say no put-back and no fault for a change by a session of that initiative.
questions: When a session of initiative i2 changes .shop/work/i2/initiative.md in the main checkout while a session of i1 works, and a later session of i2 (its gate, apply or formulate round) ends with that change still uncommitted, which requirement governs i2's own check: r218 (its own part is checked) or r215/r216 (no put-back, no fault for that change)? Reading A (r218 governs i2's own sessions; code as it is): i2's ending round puts the file back to its last commit and is taken as a fault, recorded under p2's ## Faults, with p2 keeping its status. Whether the person sees this depends on timing, so the r215 and r216 scenarios hold only when every i2 session ends before the write. Reading B (r215/r216 govern every session, i2's own included): no session of i1 or i2 is faulted and the file stays as i2's session left it. work run must then tell, in i2's check, a change made by an i2 session while an i1 session worked from one it must put back under r218. That needs a record of the change's writer, which the code does not keep, and a change in Faults.checkout_changes.
